title: Introduce cost-path-synchronizer mini-batcher and quant-horizon probe
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds an experimental tenant-level batch synchronizer and a lightweight quant evaluation probe (quant-horizon) that can be toggled via feature flag. Expected cost savings on microburst workloads; rollout gated behind flag and telemetry alerts.
description: Context: Tenants with short, high-amplitude spikes were incurring disproportionate token costs because default batching and quant defaults were tuned for steady-state throughput. Motivation: provide an automated, low-risk path to align per-tenant batch shapes and quant presets to observed traffic "trajectories" without requiring manual profile ops. What this PR does: introduces a new Cost Path Synchronizer (Syncer) that coordinates a miniature prefill/mini-batcher with the serving scheduler and a Quant-Horizon Probe that periodically evaluates candidate quantization presets over short sliding windows and reports expected token-cost vs quality tradeoffs. The Syncer computes tenant-specific horizon windows, groups incoming requests into micro-batches when beneficial, and enforces budget-aware deadlines to avoid violating latency SLOs. The Quant-Horizon Probe runs ephemeral evaluation jobs (1-3s windows) using lightweight sampling and a shadow-compare against the tenant's pinned model variant; results are surfaced to the Console and used to suggest safe quant presets. Key implementation notes: a new src/scheduler/cost_syncer.go implements a cost-aware batching policy and KV-cache hints; src/batcher/mini_prefill.go contains the mini-batcher and prefill heuristics; tools/quant_horizon/* implements the probe harness and the probe-runner service; console: ui/tenant_defaults/cost_syncer_panel.tsx and api routes for toggling flags; CLI: rwdctl cost-scan --tenant <id> --dryrun to run the probe on demand. Summary of commits: (1) scaffold Syncer + config and integration with scheduler; (2) mini-batcher implementation + prefill policies; (3) quant-horizon probe + probe runner; (4) telemetry/metrics hooks and unit_econ metrics; (5) Console UI and API; (6) CLI command and docs; (7) tests and lint fixes. Representative changed files: src/scheduler/cost_syncer.go, src/batcher/mini_prefill.go, tools/quant_horizon/probe_runner.go, ui/tenant_defaults/cost_syncer_panel.tsx, cli/rwdctl/cost_scan.go, tests/integration/tenant_sync_burst_test.go, tests/integration/quant_horizon_smoke_test.go, charts/featureflags.yaml, docs/ops/cost-sync-runbook.md. Small illustrative diff snippet: "@@ src/scheduler/cost_syncer.go @@ func chooseBatchWindow() { // new heuristic uses tenantTrafficSlope and budgetDeadline }". Performance & cost signal: internal simulator (based on traces from three seed tenants) shows token-cost reduction of 6-18% for bursty workloads and p99 latency improvements of 10-25% when mini-batcher is allowed to aggregate short windows; median latency impact is <3% in steady state. Safety & fallback: Syncer defaults to conservative thresholds; if Quant-Horizon probe fails or reports quality degradation >1.5% on our eval metrics the runtime automatically reverts to pinned model/quant configuration. A new flag redwood.enable_cost_sync (default: false) and per-tenant override controls rollout. Rollout plan: feature flagged, canary to 10 tenants for 48h, expand to 25% after telemetry verification, then global; monitor unit_econ.delta, tenant.error_rate, and p99 latency dashboards. Review conversation highlights: Kai Chen: "Need an explicit CPU/IO budget for the probe runner to avoid noisy neighbor effects; prefer cgroup-based limit." Author reply (Ava): "Added probe CPU cap (0.1 core by default) and probe PID isolation; documented in charts/featureflags.yaml." Jordan Patel: "Add a CLI dry-run and ensure no persisted state is written for probe-only runs." Author: "Implemented rwdctl cost-scan --dryrun, added integration test to assert no DB writes." Riley Thompson: "Expand telemetry to track tenant_unit_cost_delta and probe_quality_score over time." Author: "Added tenant_metric.unit_cost_delta and probe_quality.score; updated Console panel to visualize them." CI & testing: CI passed (build/test/lint) after one flaky integration test (quant_horizon_smoke_test) failed on first run due to timing; rerun succeeded. Files changed count small and focused to core scheduler, batcher, tools, console and docs. Merge: squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-20 by Ava Martinez. Migration / operational steps: operators should enable redwood.enable_cost_sync=false by default, flip for selected tenants using Console or rwdctl, watch the new unit_econ.alert (threshold configurable) and revert if unit cost increases unexpectedly. Related work: ENG-4021 (mini-batcher design), ENG-4090 (quant probe harness). No breaking changes. Notes: this PR intentionally ships as experimental with feature flag and conservative defaults; follow-up work planned: automated per-tenant rollout recommendations and integration with Optimize suggestions engine.
